candidate.title: P^3: Joint Program-and-Proof Planning for Verified Code Generation

verified_claims: Across Verina, AlgoVeri, and Lean4Commit0 with four frontier LLM backends, P^3 reports the highest solve rate in all 12 benchmark-model cells.
Compared with the stronger primary baseline, reported solve-rate gains are 4.6 to 11.2 percentage points.

The targeted implementation-only-planning ablation reports P^3 gains of 3.3 to 8.3 percentage points, directly supporting the marginal value of jointly planning program and proof rather than planning only the implementation.

On difficult-task subsets, the paper reports API-cost reduction up to roughly 40% and wall-clock reduction up to roughly 37%; these efficiency claims are subset-scoped and should not be generalized to all tasks.
Lean4Commit0 is repository-derived from 108 open-source libraries and contains relational API specifications, improving task breadth relative to only textbook-style verified-code benchmarks.
important_limits: The clean worker records one run per task/model/method and no within-task variance estimate; the paper is therefore not evidence of robust multi-seed effect size.
The paper is very recent and no independent replication was verified in this comparator pass.
The strongest causal evidence isolates joint planning versus implementation-only planning, not every individual internal component of the P^3 workflow.
Efficiency gains are reported on a difficult subset and must remain scoped to that selection protocol.
No public code/artifact repository was independently verified in this pass, so reproducibility-artifact credit remains limited.

assessment.reason: Primary v1 directly verifies the cross-model/cross-benchmark quantitative gains and a targeted Plan-Seq versus P^3 ablation that isolates joint program-and-proof planning. Evidence is strong for this scoped mechanism, but the study is a very recent preprint with single-run cells, no verified independent replication, and limited artifact verification; keep A- rather than A.
assessment.scope: Joint program-and-proof planning for Lean verified-code generation on the reported Verina, AlgoVeri, and Lean4Commit0 configurations and four frontier backends. Do not generalize to theorem proving broadly, smaller open models, repeated-run reliability, or all efficiency regimes.
